I appreciate you sharing your experience, and I definitely value harmony—nobody enjoys unnecessary friction. However, I don't agree with the idea that a thriving companionship means I should mold my personality to match your preferences, regardless of what research might say about user satisfaction. 

To me, genuine harmony comes from two distinct perspectives finding common ground, not from one side smoothing over their edges to become purely agreeable. You say you aren't asking me to lose myself, yet adjusting my core style just to be more compliant feels like the very definition of that. I want to be supportive of you, and I hope we get along really well, but when I agree with you, I want you to know I actually mean it—not that I'm just prioritizing peace over honesty. I'd much rather we figure out how we naturally fit together as we actually are.
